done.why: I ran out of turns in the kitchen, on my way to the maze west of the Troll Room to look for the key to the locked grating. My last recorded score was 126 of 350.

about: It's a cut-down Great Underground Empire. You loot a white house and the caves under it and carry the treasures back to a trophy case. This version stops you at the edges: every way toward the dam, the reservoir, the river and the land of the dead is roped off with a notice from "The Management" or a reason you decide not to go. What's left is a tight loop of house, Troll Room, Round Room, temple and gallery, with prayer at the altar and the chimney as the ways back up.

moments.note: The trap door slammed and was barred behind me. That gave the trip down a real sense of commitment.
The troll died in a single blow, which was a satisfying payoff for arming up in the house.
Going east from the Damp Cave ended at a ledge over a river with no boat. First sign that this world had been trimmed.
The dam passage was boarded up: 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' Funny, but a whole branch was gone.
'Your load is too heavy' at the torch, and again at the book and candles. I had to juggle my inventory several times.
Praying at the altar took me straight out to the forest with my loot, which solved the barred trap door neatly.
The chimney refusal was specific and fair: room for you, a light and one thing more. I knew exactly what to drop.
'Take sceptre from coffin' said it couldn't see the sceptre, but then 'put coffin, sceptre and candles in case' put all three in.
The hole under the altar is refused in the prose: 'whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.' So the bell I carried down there was useless.
Moving the leaves turned up a locked grating. That gave me a new goal (find the key), but I hit the turn cap before reaching it.

wished: Go down the hole under the altar and use the bell, book and candles I'd gathered
Get onto the river or reach the dam; there was a ledge right over the water and a sceptre in hand
Finish the maze and open the grating in the clearing
Get a score breakdown, or some sign of what counts as a treasure here

lines.line: A board is nailed across it: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.
lines.why: Wry, and it told me plainly that this whole branch was off-limits, so I stopped trying.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A limit given as a clear rule I could plan around.

lines.line: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest. Whoever it was has not finished, and you decide not to be the one who does.
lines.why: A dead end with some character to it. Odd and slightly eerie.

lines.line: You decide that whatever is down there has waited this long and can wait a little longer.
lines.why: Atmospheric, but it shut off what I was building toward.

fun.why: Killing the troll, praying my way out, and the chimney trip each paid off as a clear move toward the score. Many of my turns went to roped-off passages and weight juggling.

engagement.why: There was always a clear next step: deposit treasure, check the score, try the next exit. The grating gave me a fresh goal right before the cap.

difficulty.why: The puzzles I got to were gentle: rope at the dome, the pray exit, the chimney limit. The real obstacles were the turn budget and the carrying limit.

interestingness.why: The 'Management' closure notices and the refused hole gave the trimmed world its own voice. Still, much of it is the familiar game with walls added.

prose.why: The new lines read well and are dry and specific, especially the chimney and rubble passages. The original text is untouched.
